newsitem.title: UK: Euro crude buyers gear up for fresh Iraqi exports.
newsitem.headline: Euro crude buyers gear up for fresh Iraqi exports.

text.p: European oil traders said on Thursday that they expect to start lifting Iraqi crude under the second period of the United Nations barter agreement in two to three weeks.
The United Nations renewed the "oil-for-food" deal on Wednesday, allowing Iraq to sell another $2-billion of crude over six-months to raise cash to buy food, medicines and other goods.
Traders said they expected the process of contract signings and approvals to take at least 10 days from June 8, the first day of the renewed programme.

"If you consider one week to sign and approve all the contracts and then two or three days to arrange the first ship, we should see the first liftings from both ports (Ceyhan on the Mediterranean and Mina Al-Bakr in the Gulf) by June 18-20," said one regular lifter of Iraqi crude.
But another said that inevitable glitches meant that exports were unlikely to resume until "well into the third decade".

Unlike last December when the original contracts were signed, Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) is unlikely to ask crude lifters to make the long road trip to Baghdad to renew their orders, traders said.
"SOMO doesn't need another visit from customers, a telex is enough," said one trader.
But new players seeking oil would probably be required to meet the Iraqis face-to-face, they said.

Without an uptick in world oil prices -- which have tumbled more than five dollars a barrel since the U.N. deal got underway last December -- export volumes in the second six-month period will rise to meet the $2 billion revenue target.
Several lifters from the first six-month programme said they would like to hike their contract volumes but some said that extra barrels are likely to be allocated to Russian companies.

"Many people are trying to increase their volumes. But if they give more they are likely to give it to the Russians... They have strong business connections upstream and strong political connections," a Mediterranean refiner said.
Most European traders believed the pricing structure for Kirkuk blend would remain unchanged in the second programme.
The price for Kirkuk, indexed to Saudi Arab Light crude, would be around Dated Brent -$2.00 a barrel for June liftings and Dated Brent -$2.20 in July, they said.
"At the moment Arab Light is absolutely in line with the market so the mechanism is good for us," said one buyer. "But this can change if the (Arab Light) price moves out of synch."
